text:
mina: FYI escalated — ACME reporting EU users seeing spikes in latency and a bunch of 502/401s. They also saw a billing jump. Root says requests from FR are landing in us-west-2.
ryan: copying logs? any common trace ids?
mina: paste logs from their trace: ```trace=9a3f7c
incoming_ip=84.23.11.4 (FR)
routed_region=us-west-2
route_policy=failover:{priority:[\"us-west-2\",\"eu-west-1\"] weights:[\"100\",\"0\"] sticky:true ttl:3600}
response=502 gateway
auth_error=token-signature-invalid (intermittent)
```  
aj: that route_policy looks wrong — weights are stringified. we had a parsing change in the console last week that treats missing numeric parse as 0 then reorders priority list when building the seed hash.
elaine: timeline — a console commit went live ~18:55 UTC that changed how the policy JSON is serialized for multi-region policies. deploy-bot noted canary at 18:58: `deploy-bot: canary-policy-commit 0xabcde -> routing-ui`.
deploy-bot: policy-apply: commit=0xabcde scope=console canary=10% status=complete
mina: customer repro steps (from their ops):
1) set region header `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1`
2) run 50 concurrent requests over 30s
3) observe ~60% routed to us-west with 502s and some 401s on followups
Command they used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' -v
```
ryan: quick hypothesis — sticky cookie TTL + new priority/hashseed logic caused initial failover to choose us-west (weight parse -> default 0), cookie set domain mismatch caused subsequent requests to stick to us-west then auth was failing because HMAC key rotation differs per region.
elaine: agreed. also saw UI showing priority order as [eu-west-1, us-west-2] but runtime compiled it as [us-west-2, eu-west-1] (ordering flip). looks like an insertion sort bug when weight==0.
aj: repro locally with the serialized policy from the UI and runtime: pasted serialized policy from their org settings: ```{"priority":["eu-west-1","us-west-2"],"weights":["0","100"],"sticky":true}```. runtime interpreted weights as ints -> [0,100] so it favored us-west.
mina: immediate ask from ACME: rollback policy change, reduce TTL, and patch auth to accept rotated keys until we fix config parsing. can we do an emergency rollback?
ryan: I pushed a rollback to routing-config at 19:03 UTC (commit 0xabcde -> revert 0xabcdf). Applied config patch to treat weights as numbers and added a migration that coerces string->int. For emergency mitigation I forced policy generation to prefer explicit priority array if weights parse to zero.
deploy-bot: policy-apply: commit=0xabcdf revert=0xabcde status=applied target=global
billing: FYI billing spike is visible: +18% token egress for ACME org from wrong-region egress. We should issue credit while we sort root cause.
mina: applied workaround for ACME (reverted, forced rollout to their org, lowered sticky ttl to 60s). They confirmed in chat that latencies dropped and requests are hitting eu-west-1 again.
aj: follow-ups: 1) add unit tests for string weights and ordering, 2) add console warning when serializing weights as strings, 3) add a migration that rewrites existing policies where weights are strings and priority order ambiguous.
elaine: opened PS-1124 for migration + PS-1125 for console serialization fix. tagging infra to audit key rotation per-region.
mina: closing loop with customer now — offered credit and will send postmortem. I'll update support ticket and close once billing confirms credit.
billing: noted, will prepare credit memo for ACME and flag org for manual review.\n
